subject.declared_domain: NFRA_CSE.P3 -- the DEPLOY producer: deploy-completion ledger legs -> DEPLOY CSEs into the C0 log. Implements the certed contract_deploy (ProducerKind.DEPLOY, ref = the ledger id, compiler deploy-ledger-compiler, recognizer deploy_ledger_recognizer over org/critical_paths/change_management/*_deploy_completion.md, verb = create). Its declared discipline is HIGH-PRECISION-ONLY typing: a typed subject requires a lexically CERTAIN resource name, and anything ambiguous degrades to Concept(untyped)+low rather than inventing a type.

methodology.how: glob(org/critical_paths/change_management/*_deploy_completion.md), optionally sliced to the last --limit. For each ledger, _LEG_ROW (a multiline regex requiring the CLOSED state) yields (leg_id, kind, target, proof, state); recognize_resource runs five ORDERED high-precision patterns over target+proof and returns the first match. A leg resolving a NOT-yet-seen resource emits a typed CSE at confidence 1.0; a leg resolving nothing emits ONE Concept(untyped)+0.2 CSE, gated on the ledger having emitted nothing YET; every other leg is dropped by `else: continue`. The batch is validated fail-closed via cse_store.validate_batch (any rejection prints up to 15 and returns 1 WITHOUT writing) and written to --out as JSONL.

key.identity_space: CSE event ids in the DEPLOY namespace, scoped per (ledger, leg, resolved-subject) rather than per deploy. The producer ref is the ledger slug, which crosses from the change-management record space into the CSE producer space unchanged.
key.key_expression: EVENT ID: f'deploy:{slug}:{leg_id}:{subj_ref}'[:180] (:89), where slug = basename minus '_deploy_completion.md' (:75) and subj_ref is either the recognized resource ref or f'deploy:{slug}:<unresolved>' (:85) -- so on the untyped path the slug appears TWICE in one id. SUBJECT REF: the first non-empty group of the first matching pattern, via _first_group (:57-58). PRODUCER REF: the ledger slug (:91). THE 180-CHAR TRUNCATION IS A REAL BUT UNEXERCISED HAZARD, AND IT IS SIZED RATHER THAN ASSERTED: measured over the 13 live rows, event_id length runs 61..137, so the worst live case sits 43 characters under the cap and NONE is at it. Because the untyped form doubles the slug, a slug of roughly 72+ characters would reach the cap; the longest slug observed is 49. A collision would present as the store's event_id idempotency filter silently skipping a row, not as an error -- so it is worth knowing about, but it has not happened and is not near happening.
key.declared_mapping: The recognizer set and its first-match-wins ordering are declared in the comment at :42-46, with the reasoning ('a wrong-typed subject is worse than an honest-degrade') and the deliberate exclusion of free-text tokens. NOT DECLARED: the 180-character truncation; and the module docstring's account of WHEN the untyped CSE is emitted is looser than the code -- see failure_mode.
key.evidence: Expressions read at :75, :85, :89, :91, :57-58. failure_mode.returns_on_failure: FAIL-CLOSED ON VALIDATION, ZERO LOCAL HANDLERS. An AST handler census returns 0 except-handlers in this module, so an unreadable ledger file (open at :73) or a schema import failure (:37) PROPAGATES -- the module never converts a RAISED exception into a value. I originally wrote 'a missing ledger directory' into that same list and my credit census falsified it: glob.glob returns [] rather than raising, so a missing or RENAMED ledger directory never becomes an exception at all -- see the silent-degrade paths. Validation is fail-closed at :136-140 (rejection prints up to 15 and returns 1 with NO file write), and cse_store's own ingest path re-validates and aborts rather than writing a partial batch (:468-480). THE REAL FAILURE MODE IS NOT AN EXCEPTION -- IT IS A HANDOFF NOBODY COMPLETES, AND IT HAS ALREADY HAPPENED. Neither route is scheduled at the producer end, and the table shows the outcome: one append on 2026-07-08 and silence for 53 days. On Route A the nightly sweep prints batches=0 and exits clean when the lane is empty, so an empty lane and a healthy quiet night are the same observable.
silent_degrade_paths: AN EMPTY OR MISSING CORPUS IS A CLEAN SUCCESS. glob.glob returns [] for a missing or renamed ledger directory (EXERCISED: [] for a non-existent dir, 464 ledgers for the real one as the positive control), and cse_store.validate_batch([]) returns ([], []) without raising (EXERCISED). Nothing between :126 and :147 guards an empty ledger list, so the run prints 'OK: 0/0 DEPLOY CSEs PASS fail-closed validation', WRITES AN EMPTY JSONL over --out, prints 'wrote 0', and returns 0. A relocated ledger directory, a changed filename convention and a genuine absence of CLOSED legs are one observable, and the rc is the success rc. This is the same shape as the module's other failures: the loud paths are guarded and the quiet ones return 0.

THE UNTYPED FALLBACK IS ORDER-DEPENDENT, NOT CONTENT-DEPENDENT, AND THE DOCSTRING SAYS OTHERWISE. Docstring :12-14 declares 'a ledger contributes a Concept-untyped deploy CSE if it names no resolvable resource'. The code condition at :83 is `elif ent is None and not out`, evaluated leg by leg -- so a ledger whose FIRST leg does not resolve emits the untyped row even when a LATER leg resolves cleanly. EXERCISED on the live batch: 2 of the 10 ledgers carry BOTH an L1 Concept(untyped)+0.2 row AND typed rows from L2/L3 (nfra-cse-p2-c0-log-land -> L1 untyped + L2 Service globgrph-derive-build + L3 Table globgrph.cse; nfra-infrpt-p3-producer-fold-derive -> L1 untyped + L2 Service). Those untyped rows assert that the resource is not lexically resolvable from a ledger the recognizer resolved two legs later

verdict.why: The recognizer is the most disciplined thing IN THIS MODULE and the card should say so precisely -- I first wrote 'on this face', which is a comparative over four subjects of which I have carded two, and my credit census caught it. Five patterns declared high-precision-only with the reasoning in the source; a refusal of bare free-text tokens that I exercised with a live 7-member negative arm and a 5-member positive arm rather than quoting the comment; an honest-degrade instead of an invented type; and fail-closed validation on both the local run and the ingest. Its handler count is zero, but that buys less than it appears -- see the blocking defect on the empty corpus. QUALIFIED on four measured points. FIRST, AND IT IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS: nothing schedules this producer on either of its two routes, and the table shows the cost -- source=deploy holds ONE append of 13 rows dated 2026-07-08, the day the module was authored, and nothing in the 53 days since. The partition census splits the five producers exactly along the line the code structure predicts: the two that run on the scheduled Fargate task are current to 2026-08-30, the two LOCAL-source ones fired once at authoring, and a fifth has never landed a row at all. SECOND, an exercised correctness defect: the untyped fallback is gated on `not out` rather than on the ledger's content, so 2 of 10 live ledgers carry a Concept(untyped) row asserting the resource is unresolvable alongside typed rows the recognizer resolved two legs later -- the docstring describes content-dependent behaviour the code does not implement. THIRD, 77% of everything this producer has ever emitted is that untyped fallback. FOURTH, legs are dropped uncounted while the printed denominator is ledgers. I record two of my own instrument failures on this card rather than only its subject's: a --query KeyCount projection that returned a false zero on a prefix I had proven non-empty, and a positive control that failed because I passed the wrong prefix string. Neither reached a finding, and only because the controls ran. My first draft of this card also carried a systematic off-by-one across roughly a dozen line citations, drafted from an earlier read instead of from the file, and every citation here was re-derived.
